approval_required_for: Binding or changing tile sizes for any pipeline stage.
Binding or changing parallelism, unroll factors, PE counts, or stage replication.
Binding or changing memory layout, buffering depth, data packing, stream width, or beat alignment.
Binding or changing AXI/DDR access patterns, burst scheduling, memory schedule, or runtime transfer policy.
Any numeric-policy specialization including data type, accumulator width, rounding, saturation, quantization, or tolerance-related behavior.
Any major template specialization or template-parameter choice that changes architecture-level behavior.
expected_evidence: A parameter-binding artifact must be produced and attached to the SACG, mapping each pipeline stage to explicit design-space parameters such as tile sizes, unroll/parallelism factors, buffering depths, stream widths, packing choices, and memory/runtime assumptions where applicable.

The produced bindings must reference the originating design-space, template-selection, pipeline-plan, model-shape, numeric-policy, target-board, and tool-profile artifacts rather than introducing untraced constants.

A later parameter/static checker must verify model-order preservation, no GQA-to-MHA semantic collapse, shape consistency, numeric-policy consistency, stream/beat alignment, buffer capacity, flow-control/liveness, memory schedule feasibility, and board/tool limits.
Evidence must show the existing pipeline_plan_static_check pass remains applicable or is superseded by a new checker result after parameters are bound.

Any architectural binding that affects tile size, parallelism, memory layout, data packing, AXI/DDR access, numeric policy, or major template specialization must be recorded for human approval before downstream implementation is considered accepted.
decision.reason: The parameter_binding stage is a deterministic planning/binding step that consumes the existing SACG state and prior pipeline plan/static-check artifacts to create candidate parameter-to-stage bindings. It is not requesting deletion of tests, golden-output edits, tolerance loosening, checker bypass, or model-semantics changes. Future checker and approval evidence will still be required before any bound tile sizes, parallelism, buffering, memory layout, data packing, or runtime/AXI choices are treated as accepted design decisions.
risks: Parameter binding can silently turn abstract pipeline stages into architecture-level decisions that affect tile size, parallelism, memory layout, data packing, buffering, AXI/DDR behavior, and runtime scheduling.
Cross-layer mismatch risk between model shapes, Qwen2 attention/GQA semantics, stream ordering, beat alignment, and selected template parameters.
Board and tool-resource risk if chosen parameters exceed memory bandwidth, BRAM/URAM/DSP capacity, timing feasibility, or supported tool protocols.
Numeric risk if bindings imply data width, accumulation, quantization, rounding, or tolerance behavior not permitted by the numeric policy.
Liveness/deadlock risk if buffer depths and flow-control bindings are inconsistent across residual, branch, and join stages.
